chunks: As for the lovers of Allah, their conviction serves them as light,
and the direction of the right path serves as their guide;
while the enemies of Allah, in time of doubt call to misguidance,
One who fears death cannot escape it,
nor can one who loves it secure eternal life.

key_terms.الشُّبْهَةُ: Doubt or uncertainty that resembles truth
key_terms.سَمْتُ الْهُدَى: The path or direction of guidance

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the lovers of God and the enemies of God in times of doubt according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali defines 'shubhah' (doubt) not as mere uncertainty, but as a deceptive resemblance to truth that confuses the uninitiated; this distinction is central to Shia epistemology regarding the clarity of the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance. The passage contrasts the 'certainty' (yaqin) of the awliya with the 'blindness' (amya) of the a'da, linking spiritual perception to one's ultimate fate. It concludes with a profound paradox: those who fear death cling to it, while those who love it are denied permanence, reflecting the Shia view of death as a transition to the barzakh rather than an intermediate realm.

en.sayed-ali-raza: As for lovers of Allāh, their conviction serves them as light
and the direction of the right path (itself) serves as their guide;
while the enemies of Allāh, in time of doubt call to misguidance in the darkness of doubt
(of intelligence). One who fears death cannot escape it
nor can one who fears for eternal life secure it.
